# Bun v1.4.3

Jarred Sumner

October 10, 2026

#### To install Bun

curl

```
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
```

```
npm install -g bun
```

```
powershell -c "irm bun.sh/install.ps1|iex"
```

```
scoop install bun
```

```
brew tap oven-sh/bun
```

```
brew install bun
```

```
docker pull oven/bun
```

```
docker run --rm --init --ulimit memlock=-1:-1 oven/bun
```

#### To upgrade Bun

```
bun upgrade
```

## `bun check`: a TypeScript type checker built into Bun#

`bun check` is an incredibly fast TypeScript type checker that passes 100% of TypeScript 7.0.2's conformance test suite.

```
bun check
```

```
1 | import { greet } from "./user";
2 |
3 | const message = greet({ id: "1", name: "Ada" });
                            ^
error: TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'number'.
    at src/index.ts:3:25

Found 1 error in 1 file, checked 2 files [14.00ms]
```

It's 3x to 6.4x faster than `tsc` 7.0.2, on a 16-core Apple silicon Mac:

| Project | Files | `bun check` | `tsc` 7.0.2 | Faster |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| VS Code `src` | 9,795 | 1.24 s | 5.98 s | 4.8x |
| mikro-orm | 2,883 | 1.20 s | 5.97 s | 5.0x |
| Next.js `packages/next` | 2,881 | 0.28 s | 1.82 s | 6.4x |
| Next.js, root | 3,547 | 0.42 s | 1.28 s | 3.1x |
| Storybook `scripts` | 1,039 | 0.27 s | 0.96 s | 3.5x |
| Nuxt | 839 | 0.27 s | 0.80 s | 3.0x |
| Playwright | 706 | 0.15 s | 0.64 s | 4.2x |
| lit `packages/react` | 6 | 0.46 s | 2.12 s | 4.6x |

And it uses 2.2x to 4.9x less memory:

| Project | Files | `bun check` | `tsc` 7.0.2 | Less |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| VS Code `src` | 9,795 | 2.14 GB | 7.97 GB | 3.7x |
| mikro-orm | 2,883 | 1.35 GB | 6.67 GB | 4.9x |
| Next.js `packages/next` | 2,881 | 0.71 GB | 1.81 GB | 2.5x |
| Next.js, root | 3,547 | 0.55 GB | 1.33 GB | 2.4x |
| Storybook `scripts` | 1,039 | 0.56 GB | 1.39 GB | 2.5x |
| Nuxt | 839 | 0.51 GB | 1.14 GB | 2.2x |
| Playwright | 706 | 0.46 GB | 1.06 GB | 2.3x |
| lit `packages/react` | 6 | 0.24 GB | 0.63 GB | 2.6x |

It's a port of typescript-go. It reads your `tsconfig.json`, reports the same errors as `tsc`, and uses every CPU core. You don't need the `typescript` package installed.

It only type checks. It doesn't emit JavaScript or `.d.ts` files, and there's no language server, so your editor keeps using TypeScript.

### `bun run --check`#

Type check, then run. If there's a type error, your code doesn't run.

```
bun run --check src/index.ts
```

```
1 | import { greet } from "./user";
2 |
3 | console.log(greet({ id: "1", name: "Ada" }));
                        ^
error: TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'number'.
    at src/index.ts:3:21

2 |   id: number;
      ^
note: The expected type comes from property 'id' which is declared here on type 'User'
   at src/user.ts:2:3

Found 1 error in 1 file, checked 2 files [24.00ms]
```

It also works with `package.json` scripts (`bun run --check dev`) and with `--watch`, which checks again before every restart.

### `bun test --check`#

Type check the test files and everything they import, then run the tests. If there's a type error, no tests run.

```
bun test --check
```

```
bun test v1.4.3
4 | test("greet", () => {
5 |   expect(greet({ id: "1", name: "Ada" })).toBe("hello Ada");
                     ^
error: TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'number'.
    at src/user.test.ts:5:18

2 |   id: number;
      ^
note: The expected type comes from property 'id' which is declared here on type 'User'
   at src/user.ts:2:3

Found 1 error in 1 file, checked 2 files [23.94ms]
```

### `bun build --check`#

Type check, then bundle. A type error fails the build like any other build error, and nothing is written.

```
bun build --check ./src/index.ts --outdir out
```

```
3 | console.log(greet({ id: "1", name: "Ada" }));
                        ^
error: TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'number'.
    at /app/src/index.ts:3:21

2 |   id: number;
      ^
note: TS6

results.text:
TLS fixes, faster bun check, memory leak fix · Changelog

 oven-sh/bun · October 10th, 2026 · 5 commits 

# TLS fixes, faster bun check, memory leak fix

Big TLS consolidation, two bun check performance/correctness fixes, and a Blob ownership leak fix.

### Major TLS hardening and API/docs cleanup (6c1eb06)

Bun consolidated a large batch of TLS fixes across `fetch`, `node:tls`, `node:https`, WebSocket, and SQL, with new/clarified certificate handling and SNI behavior. The docs and types now cover `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, mTLS `requestCert`, `rejectUnauthorized`, CRLs, Redis `serverName`, and stricter SQL SSL-mode precedence, so TLS configuration is both more capable and less ambiguous.

### Fix Blob string ownership leaks on dropped bodies (1f6987c)

`blob::Any` now owns its string arm correctly, so dropping a rejected `fetch()`/`Bun.spawn`/shell body releases the underlying string instead of leaking a ref. This closes a significant RSS growth bug and adds regression coverage for the affected request/body paths.

### Make bun check handle deep interface chains in linear time (c6da4a4)

Type relation and shape instantiation now avoid cubic blowups on long inheritance chains, which cuts `bun check` time dramatically on generated typings and similar code. The change also adds a targeted benchmark-style regression test to guard the fast path.

### Fix bun check error handling and per-file flow state (d2035cc)

`bun check --threads=1` no longer masks real errors, and files that hit TS2563-style flow limits stop poisoning later files. This makes diagnostics more reliable in long files and restores correct behavior for single-threaded checks.

### Other misc changes

- Version bump (`71d0d43`)

# OSS Releases: Bun 1.4.3, Nuxt 4.6.1, LiteLLM 1.105.0 and More

This week's stable releases bring Bun 1.4.3, Nuxt 4.6.1, a wave of LangChain and LiteLLM AI tooling updates, and a broad esbuild-to-Rolldown migration across Astro adapters.

## Frameworks

- withastro/astro (@astrojs/vercel 11.0.14): Fixes on-demand routes crashing with "Cannot find native binding" on Vercel caused by serverless functions loading rolldown at runtime. Release
- withastro/astro (@astrojs/vercel 11.0.13, @astrojs/netlify 8.2.9, @astrojs/markdoc 2.0.11): Internal bundling and code transforms migrated from esbuild to Vite's Oxc-based `transformWithOxc` and Rolldown; direct esbuild dependency dropped across all three adapters. Vercel | Netlify | Markdoc
- nuxt/nuxt (v4.6.1): Broad patch release fixing Vite 8.1+ optimizer message matching, `setPageLayout` type narrowing, `Serialize` object alignment with JSON, dev handler registration, and BroadcastChannel error handling, plus a lazy-build performance win for portable event web views. Release

## Runtime

- oven-sh/bun (v1.4.3): Maintenance release with contributions from eight community members; full notes on the Bun blog. Release
- cloudflare/workerd (v1.20261013.1): Adds a `wasm_esm_integration_builtins` compat flag for runtime-compiled Wasm and groups SRS queries by a top-level `queryId`. Release
- cloudflare/workerd (v1.20261010.1): Introduces a V8 startup-snapshot pipeline, wraps the global object via `WrapGlobal`, fixes a parked alarm desynchronization bug, and upgrades to V8 15.6 compatibility. Release
- cloudflare/workerd (v1.20261009.1): Adds observer hooks for isolate cost attribution and V8 internal histograms, introduces `spanContext` for distributed tracing, and fixes multiple TypeScript readable/writable stream re-entrancy bugs. Release

## Data

- ClickHouse/ClickHouse: Patch releases across four maintained tracks this week: stable v26.9.17.8, LTS v26.8.25.14, stable v26.7.28.6, and LTS v26.3.49.3. No changelogs published; treat as bug-fix maintenance. v26.9.17.8

## AI

- openai/openai-python (v3.29.0): Adds `billing_not_active` session error code, a new "shida" named Live voice, vault metadata filters, and aligned beta pagination limits. Release
- openai/openai-python (v3.28.0): Adds agent environment suspension and expiration support. Release
- BerriAI/litellm (v1.105.0): Adds compatibility-aware MCP result conversion across tool surfaces, fixes Redis Cluster auth-cache invalidation via node-level pub/sub, and adds Rust registry validation for the model catalog. Release
- BerriAI/litellm (v1.104.3): Backports the decision model guardrail and auto-router UI setup to the stable 1.104 branch. Release
- langchain-ai/langchain (langchain 1.4.5): Adds a summarizer to `SummarizationMiddleware`. Release
- langchain-ai/langchain (langchain-openai 1.7.1, langchain-core 1.6.10, langchain-anthropic 1.7.6): Incremental bug-fix point releases across the OpenAI, Anthropic, and core integrations. langchain-openai | core | anthropic
- anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript (sdk-v0.133.0): Adds unified analytics metric types for Chat and Cowork, plus workflows, multiagent configuration, and thread-status filtering for Managed Agents. Release
- vllm-project/vllm (v0.32.0rc0): Release candidate reporting host pool in KV cache capacity logs (HiSparse). Release

## DevTools

- neovim/neovim (v0.12.6): Stable bugfix release, now the current `stable` tag; changelog linked via `:help news` inside Nvim. Release

This week's releases highlight two converging trends: the Astro ecosystem completing its move from esbuild to Rolldown signals that the Vite/Oxc toolchain is reaching production-grade adoption in major frameworks, while the volume of AI-layer updates across LiteLLM, LangChain, and the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs underscores how rapidly the agentic tooling surface area is expanding for developers

results.title: Bun lands lint/format and major check fixes · Changelog
results.text:
Bun lands lint/format and major check fixes · Changelog

 oven-sh/bun · October 12th, 2026 · 6 commits 

# Bun lands lint/format and major check fixes

Native lint/format arrive, Bun learns Yarn Berry migrations, and bun check gets a big round of tsc parity fixes.

 

`bun lint` and `bun format` go native (c39c718) Bun adds first-class linting and formatting commands with config support for ESLint/oxlint and Prettier/oxfmt-style workflows. This is a major expansion of the CLI, bringing a large built-in toolchain and new docs/tests to support it.

Yarn Berry lockfiles now migrate to `bun.lock` (d1cb7db) `bun install` can now convert Yarn 2+ lockfiles instead of rejecting them, preserving pinned versions when Bun can faithfully represent the graph. The migration handles workspaces, patches, aliases, git/tarball/file deps, catalogs, and more; when it can't preserve semantics exactly, it explains why and falls back to resolving from `package.json`.

`bun check` closes more gaps with `tsc` (b92e2f4) This fixes several correctness issues around unions/intersections, readonly/private/protected property behavior, and large `paths` configs that previously caused quadratic work. It also tightens a few remaining parity differences with TypeScript in loop/destructuring cases.

`bun check` improves circular/looped type resolution (772f87f) A broad refactor adjusts how `bun check` tracks in-progress resolutions, cached signatures, and loop visibility so it matches `tsc` on many more programs. The changes target subtle cases around recursive inference and Promise-like `then` resolution, reducing false errors and disagreement with TypeScript.

DOM constructors now validate subclassing before side effects (39bbb71) Web-facing constructors like `WebSocket`, `Worker`, and `BroadcastChannel` now read `new.target.prototype` before creating underlying resources. That prevents cases where a thrown subclassing check would otherwise leave a socket, subscription, or thread already started.

### Other misc changes

- Shared percent-encoding helpers reused in Yarn Berry migration (1 commit)
- Docs and metadata updates for new install/lint/format behavior
- Small internal refactors and test fixture updates

results.title: Bun 1.4.3 ships bun check, a TypeScript checker faster than tsc: Reveneau
results.text:
Bun 1.4.3 ships bun check, a TypeScript checker faster than tsc: Reveneau

# Bun 1.4.3 ships bun check, a TypeScript checker faster than tsc

Bun 1.4.3 adds bun check, a type checker Bun says runs 3x to 6.4x faster than tsc 7.0.2 and uses 2.2x to 4.9x less memory on real projects.

Editorial 4 days ago 3 min read

Image: Bun

Why it matters Type checking is a step most teams run on every pull request and on every save in a watcher, so a checker that is a few times faster and lighter frees that CI slot and that laptop fan for other work.

Type checking is the step a developer waits on while the editor fan spins up. Bun 1.4.3 ships its own checker and runs on a stock Next.js tree in 0.28 seconds, against 1.82 seconds for tsc 7.0.2 on the same machine.

Jarred Sumner, who created Bun, published the release. The headline feature is `bun check`, a port of typescript-go built into the runtime, and the company says it passes 100% of TypeScript 7.0.2's conformance suite: 51,210 tests across errors, types, symbols, declarations and module resolution, all passing. There is no TypeScript package to install and no language server attached, so the editor keeps using TypeScript for in-file errors while `bun check` runs the full-project pass.

## 1.24 seconds against 5.98 on the VS Code tree

Bun's own eight-row table was measured on a 16-core Apple silicon Mac. On the VS Code source tree, 9,795 files, `bun check` ran in 1.24 seconds against 5.98 seconds for tsc 7.0.2, so 4.8 times faster, and used 2.14 GB of memory against 7.97 GB, so 3.7 times less. On Playwright, 706 files, it was 4.2 times faster and used 2.3 times less memory. Across the eight projects, Bun reports 3.0x to 6.4x faster and 2.2x to 4.9x less memory.

Those are Bun's figures on Bun's own hardware. A team adopting it should re-measure on its own project before planning around them.

## Where the 72-project parity run disagreed with tsc

Bun separates three kinds of testing. The TypeScript conformance suite covers 51,210 cases, all passing. On top of that, Bun deliberately misconfigured 72 popular repositories, including drizzle-orm, hono, langchainjs, nestjs, next.js, prisma, remix, svelte, vitest and vuejs/core, and compared file, line, column and error code against tsc. The report says 71 of 72 produce identical results. The one mismatch is in vuejs/core, where tsc only reports an error when `global.ts` comes before `model.ts` in the files list.

The third track is fuzzing. The release blog says 136,235 fuzzer-generated functions run on each commit with zero mismatches, and 3,032,182 larger offline programs produce 191 mismatches, 162 of which are code that refers to itself while being declared, like `class A { x = { a: null! as { p: A["x"] } } }`. Those cases are the limit Bun is open about.

## --check runs on `bun run`, `bun test` and `bun build`

The flag `--check` plugs into `bun run`, `bun test` and `bun build`. On a type error, the code does not run, no test runs and nothing is written. `--watch` runs the check again before every restart. `Bun.build({ check: true })` carries the same flag into the programmatic API. A team can verify parity on its own tree by running `bunx tsc` and `bun check` side by side and diffing the output, the exact reproduction Bun proposes.

The release also carries runtime work. Bun says it cut idle CPU use by 67 to 89 percent on a sleeping server, added `Bun.FetchSession` for a group of requests with their own TLS, proxy and keep-alive settings, and shipped an experimental `Bun.ModuleGraph` for running several copies of one app in one process with separate module state. One hundred and sixty-six issues were closed.

For a team already in TypeScript, the slow step in local development stops being the slow step. A pre-push hook that ran tsc on a 3,547-file Next.js root in 1.28 seconds now has room for a second check in the same budget.

## Source

Bun v1.4.3 release blog, by Jarred Sumner. GitHub tag: oven-sh/bun v1.4.3. Benchmark tables, c

Bun adds built-in TypeScript checking · Changelog

 oven-sh/bun · October 6th, 2026 · 2 commits 

# Bun adds built-in TypeScript checking

Bun gains a new `check` command for TypeScript type checking, alongside a WebKit engine upgrade and compatibility fixes.

### Bun ships `bun check` as a built-in TypeScript type checker (bbdc5a5)

Bun now includes a first-class `check` command for TypeScript projects, with CLI flags, shell completions, and docs wired in. The implementation ports TypeScript Go’s checker behavior, aiming for `tsc`-compatible diagnostics and making type checking part of the same workflow as `run`, `build`, and `test`.

### Upgrade WebKit to a newer upstream snapshot (3f1765a)

Bun’s embedded WebKit/JavaScriptCore fork was bumped to upstream `dbdca7545d`, pulling in a large batch of engine changes. The update also includes internal C++ compatibility adjustments for the new `WTF::CString`/UTF-8 APIs and refreshed WebKit-specific tests, which helps keep Bun aligned with the latest engine behavior.

### Other misc changes

- Added `bun check` docs, completion support, and licensing notes.
- Updated WebKit build pinning and related test fixtures.
- Small internal binding adjustments to match upstream WebKit API changes.

results.title: Bun adds stricter builds and fixes check bugs · Changelog
results.text:
Bun adds stricter builds and fixes check bugs · Changelog

 oven-sh/bun · October 8th, 2026 · 5 commits 

# Bun adds stricter builds and fixes check bugs

New build knobs make codegen-from-strings and WebAssembly optional, while bun check lands several correctness and performance fixes.

 

### Build options add strict codegen and no-WebAssembly binaries (9ed8d11)

Bun can now be built with `codeGenerationFromStrings` and `webAssembly` disabled, making `--disallow-code-generation-from-strings=strict` a compile-time constant and removing the `WebAssembly` global in that binary. The published builds stay unchanged, but source builds can now hard-enforce stricter runtime behavior or strip wasm support entirely.

### bun check fixes conflicting exports and several false positives (620b50f)

`bun check` now handles names exported by conflicting declarations more like TypeScript, avoiding the wrong error in generated `.d.ts` files. This is a correctness fix for a real edge case in declaration-heavy packages.

### bun check fixes multiple type-analysis bugs and speeds up worst cases (4c54c9b)

This release fixes a cluster of `bun check` mismatches with `tsc`, including missing/false errors around `NoInfer`, JSDoc, long `!` chains, and repeated package copies. It also includes performance work in union/intersection property checks and related type machinery, which should help pathological inputs that previously took minutes.

### React Fast Refresh now hashes hook bindings correctly (5749c31)

The React Fast Refresh signature now includes the hook binding itself, so renaming one `useState` binding no longer collides with another. That should prevent stale state from being incorrectly preserved across edits in dev workflows.

### ByteStream now preserves buffered data when producers error (13b126f)

Native byte streams no longer collapse to an empty successful read when the producer fails after partial output, and partial buffered data is preserved instead of triggering an out-of-bounds panic. This affects streamed fetch bodies, `Bun.serve`, S3 streaming, and HTMLRewriter output, so it fixes several user-visible error-path bugs.

### Other misc changes

- Documentation for the new build-time code generation flag
- Build/config plumbing for the new `codeGenerationFromStrings` and `webAssembly` options
- Stack-safety and hashing robustness fixes in AST/type serialization
- Miscellaneous test updates
